checks.Title: Seduce, don't just observe
checks.Evidence: The prose is drenched in horror-first procedural detail — the Scarab's carapace 'landed to feed,' the vial drops, the clinical stench — but the strange-beautiful textures (the schism gravel orbiting a storm drain, the harpy riding thermals, the dead ad-panels marking Lotus territory) are brief asides buried inside long tactical/plot passages rather than moments the reader is invited to linger in and be pulled by.
checks.Fix: Slow down at least one or two of the genuinely seductive images (the gravel orbit, the Rift's leaning air, the lattice-breathing corners Levin sees) into fuller sensory beats before pivoting back to plot mechanics, so wonder precedes and outweighs procedural horror rather than flashing past it.

checks.Title: Open with the world doing its work
checks.Evidence: The opening beats (drops in the eye, the manifest, the smell of the rendering plant) are compressed into a handful of lines before the story pivots almost immediately into plot-critical material: a contested account flag, a botched recall, and within a few pages a shooting that kickstarts the entire Lotus plot. There is no unhurried commute or transaction allowed to simply exist before the plot machinery engages.
checks.Fix: Extend the pre-dawn routine (the drive, the yard smell, the manifest ritual, a mundane pickup or two) for several more beats before introducing the contested-account complication, so the world's ordinary rhythm is fully established before the plot demands attention.

checks.Title: Gloss first mentions in-voice, never dump
checks.Evidence: Terms like 'neuretics,' 'CorpoNations'-adjacent structures (Carrion, Lotus Syndicate, GLMZ), 'the Rift,' 'Resonance Zone geometry,' and 'Waxwing Neuromedia civic skin' are frequently introduced with either zero context (e.g. 'The manifest came up on his neuretics' with no orientation to what neuretics are beyond inference) or with an explicit stop-and-explain clause that reads as authorial aside rather than voice, e.g. 'Waxwing Neuromedia — the ad-overlay grid that painted storefronts with whatever a strip could afford to want' and 'the GLMZ — the sprawl everyone just called the zone.'
checks.Fix: Replace the appositive-definition pattern ('X — the Y that did Z') with details Tomas would naturally notice and think in the middle of action, letting terms like neuretics, GLMZ, and the Rift accrue meaning through use rather than through inserted glosses.

checks.Title: Never an acronym before its term
checks.Evidence: The acronym GLMZ appears repeatedly throughout the story (e.g., 'the same shape as the GLMZ,' 'the GLMZ had buyers,' 'in this city, the GLMZ') with only a vague apposition 'the sprawl everyone just called the zone' at first use, which is a nickname, not the full expansion of the letters G-L-M-Z; no in-voice gloss of what the acronym actually stands for is ever given.
checks.Fix: At first use, have a character or narration spell out the full term the letters GLMZ actually abbreviate (e.g., 'the Greater Lakes Metro Zone, GLMZ, the sprawl everyone just called the zone') before using the bare acronym again.

checks.Title: Give the POV character one human crack
checks.Evidence: Levin's flash of the photograph—'a man at thirty-one, a few years and a whole life ago, before the trade and before the drops, squinting into a sun somewhere that wasn't the GLMZ, grinning at whoever held the camera'—and Ekow's aside about his mother's name and the coast are genuine human cracks, but Tomas, the primary POV, gets no equivalent unguarded moment beyond functional references to Paz and the therapy bill.
checks.Fix: Give Tomas one beat of specific sensory memory unrelated to the plot machinery—something of his own life before the trade, the way Levin has the photograph—so the primary POV gets the same human flash as the secondary characters.

checks.Title: Land one beat past the handoff
checks.Evidence: The story does land past its plot business — the kidney return, Levin's photograph, the queue resuming — but it overshoots into multiple echoing gestures (the marker owed, Paz's therapy, the photograph, the three new pickups) rather than one quiet final beat, and the closing line 'up into the rest of the shift' functions more as thematic summary/editorializing about the grind than a single sharp image the reader carries out.
checks.Fix: Cut the accumulation of callbacks (marker, Paz, queue recap) down to one image — likely the photograph moment — and end on that alone, letting the Wagon simply pull away without narrating 'the rest of the shift' as a thesis statement.

checks.Title: Reward re-reading without requiring it
checks.Evidence: The prose delivers a fully comprehensible first-pass story (drops, route, heist-like cover-up, moral costs), but plants details that reread differently once the ending lands — Levin's early gentleness 'behind the glass,' the shoes set 'toes out' for Maisy, the storm-grate pour of Tears foreshadowed by 'that was the last time you dose on shift,' and Ekow's name/coat/machete details that echo his solitary walk to the lake at the end — none of which are required to follow the plot on a first read.

checks.Title: Elevate, don't reconstruct
checks.Evidence: The excerpt is dense, worldbuilt fiction (Tears, Splicers, Lotus Syndicate, Carrion, GLMZ) but every piece of jargon is glossed in-line at first use — 'Carrion called them Reclamation Agents. The street called them Vultures,' 'the GLMZ — the sprawl everyone just called the zone,' 'Waxwing Neuromedia civic skin — the ad-overlay grid that painted storefronts' — which reads as natural narration rather than an inserted primer, preserving the story's existing texture while giving newcomers doors in.

checks.Title: Orient through GLMZ's five pillars
checks.Evidence: The story braids all five pillars organically: neuretics deliver manifests and IdentiScan flags mid-scene; nanite carapaces ('Mama'/'the Kid') repair and harvest bodies as routine infrastructure; Ekow is a fully agentive AI-adjacent... wait, Ekow is human, but the Tears/neuretics divide (Levin's drug-augmented driving vs Tomas's neuretic overlays) marks the cognitive-augmentation class divide, Carrion operates as the de facto governing law over financed bodies, and the Schism appears physically ('a two-inch orbit of gravel turned slowly in the air — a little schism, months old' and 'the white gap every map printed... the air beyond it leaning in a direction that made Tomas put his eyes back on the road').
checks.Fix: Introduce at least one clearly agentive AI faction with its own stakes (distinct from human characters and background tech) so pillar one isn't left implicit through absence, since Ekow, Levin, and Tomas are all human and the AI presence is currently confined to passive tools like Mama and IdentiScan.
